title: 09. Write a performance monitoring context manager

examples.input: Three operations of 2.2 seconds on the same date
examples.explanation: The third violation reaches the daily alert threshold.

test_public_configuration_and_counter.title: test_public_configuration_and_counter
test_public_configuration_and_counter.code:
def test_public_configuration_and_counter(clock):
    assert performance.OPERATION_THRESHOLD_IN_SECONDS == 2.2
    assert performance.ALERT_THRESHOLD == 3
    assert performance.ALERT_MSG == 'ALERT: suffering performance hit today'
    assert isinstance(performance.violations, Counter)

test_alert_starts_on_third_violation.title: test_alert_starts_on_third_violation
test_alert_starts_on_third_violation.code:
def test_alert_starts_on_third_violation(clock, capsys):
    for expected in (1, 2):
        operate(clock, 3)
        assert performance.violations[clock.day] == expected
        assert capsys.readouterr().out == ''
    operate(clock, 3)
    assert performance.violations[clock.day] == 3
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == performance.ALERT_MSG + '\n'

test_each_later_violation_alerts_but_fas.title: test_each_later_violation_alerts_but_fast_operations_do_not
test_each_later_violation_alerts_but_fas.code:
def test_each_later_violation_alerts_but_fast_operations_do_not(clock, capsys):
    performance.violations[clock.day] = 3
    operate(clock, 4)
    operate(clock, 1)
    operate(clock, 5)
    assert performance.violations[clock.day] == 5
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == (performance.ALERT_MSG + '\n') * 2

test_dates_keep_independent_counts.title: test_dates_keep_independent_counts
test_dates_keep_independent_counts.code:
def test_dates_keep_independent_counts(clock, capsys):
    first = clock.day
    performance.violations[first] = 3
    clock.day = real_date(2026, 10, 29)
    operate(clock, 3)
    assert performance.violations == {first: 3, clock.day: 1}
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == ''
    clock.day = first
    operate(clock, 3)
    assert performance.violations[first] == 4
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == performance.ALERT_MSG + '\n'

test_operation_crossing_midnight_uses_ex.title: test_operation_crossing_midnight_uses_exit_date
test_operation_crossing_midnight_uses_ex.code:
def test_operation_crossing_midnight_uses_exit_date(clock, capsys):
    entry_day = clock.day
    exit_day = real_date(2026, 10, 29)
    performance.violations[exit_day] = 2
    with performance.timeit():
        clock.now += 3
        clock.day = exit_day
    assert performance.violations == {exit_day: 3}
    assert entry_day not in performance.violations
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == performance.ALERT_MSG + '\n'

test_failed_slow_operation_is_counted_an.title: test_failed_slow_operation_is_counted_and_error_propagates[error_type0]
test_failed_slow_operation_is_counted_an.code:
@pytest.mark.parametrize('error_type', [ValueError, KeyboardInterrupt])
def test_failed_slow_operation_is_counted_and_error_propagates(clock, capsys, error_type):
    failure = error_type('operation failed')
    performance.violations[clock.day] = 2
    with pytest.raises(error_type) as caught:
        with performance.timeit():
            clock.now += 3
            raise failure
    assert caught.value is failure
    assert performance.violations[clock.day] == 3
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == performance.ALERT_MSG + '\n'

test_failed_fast_operation_is_not_counte.title: test_failed_fast_operation_is_not_counted
test_failed_fast_operation_is_not_counte.code:
def test_failed_fast_operation_is_not_counted(clock, capsys):
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match='fast failure'):
        with performance.timeit():
            clock.now += 1
            raise RuntimeError('fast failure')
    assert performance.violations == {}
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == ''

test_nested_operations_use_their_own_ent.title: test_nested_operations_use_their_own_entry_time
test_nested_operations_use_their_own_ent.code:
def test_nested_operations_use_their_own_entry_time(clock, capsys):
    with performance.timeit():
        clock.now += 1
        with performance.timeit():
            clock.now += 1
        clock.now += 1
    assert performance.violations == {clock.day: 1}
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == ''

courseHelp.title: Course help
courseHelp.body:
Write your implementation above the supplied tests. Run checks the sample tests. Submit checks all supplied tests. Keep the tests and runner unchanged.

For an older saved solution, use **+** beside the editor tabs to open the current template. Copy your implementation into the new tab. Your old tab stays in place.

This template and these tests are recreated from the public description. The local API and extra input guarantees are stated in the problem. Recreated local API. Every later violation alerts. Counts use the exit date. Tests use a fake clock and date; no waiting is required. Use Python 3.11 and the standard library.

[Original Pybites exercise](https://pybitesplatform.com/bites/write-a-performance-monitoring-context-manager/)
